text:
ria: hey team, first day — I accepted the GitHub org invite through Okta but when I try to clone the onboarding repo I get 404. I can see the org on github.com but not the repos. also trying to push from my laptop errors with 'permission denied (publickey)'. any quick checks? :wave:

samir: welcome! quick Q — did you accept the invite with your work email (the one people-ops used) or a personal account?

ria: I clicked the invite link from my work email, but my browser was already logged into my personal github (personal@email.com). I think the invite opened in that session.

maria: this is usually the classic personal vs org account mismatch. Two things: 1) confirm SSO/Okta authorization on the correct github account, 2) check which SSH key is being presented by your ssh agent. run `ssh -T git@github.com` and paste the output.

ria: output: "Hi Ria! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access." — wait that suggests it's my personal account showing. but `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/onboard-starter.git` gives 404.

samir: yep that means your local key is associated with a different GH username. If the personal account has the same SSH key, GitHub will show you as that user for auth. Steps: A) remove/move the SSH key from your personal account (github.com/settings/ssh-and-gpg) B) add a new key to your work account, or generate a new key and add it to the correct account.

ria: I added my key ages ago to personal. don't want to delete it without confirming. is there a way to see which account a key belongs to?

maria: you can check by going to your personal account settings -> SSH and seeing the key fingerprint. Locally run `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` (or whatever key file) to get the fingerprint and match. Another quick debug: `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -v" git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/onboard-starter.git` will print which key ssh tries.

ria: ran the verbose clone; it attempted id_rsa -> id_ed25519 and then offered a key with fingerprint that matches my personal account entry. ok.

samir: since the personal account grabbed the key, two options: 1) remove that key from personal and add to work (fast), 2) create a new keypair for work and add only to work account (preferred), 3) use HTTPS with a personal access token but that's not ideal for org repos.

ria: would people-ops need to re-send the invite if I switch keys? i already accepted, just can't see repo.

people-ops: you won't need a new invite if SSO is tied to the correct GH account. If you accidentally accepted the invite into the wrong GH account, we can reassign — ping us and we can revoke and re-invite to the right email. Before that, try the key switch flow and authorizing SSO: go to https://github.com/organizations/redwood-inference/sso to confirm your work account has granted SSO to the org.

ria: I removed the key from my personal account and added a new ed25519 to my work account. after reauthing Okta and the SSO prompt I can see the repo now. cloning works and `git push` to my fork succeeded. :tada:

maria: excellent. one more prophylactic: add a ~/.ssh/config entry pointing Host github.com to the correct IdentityFile for your work key to avoid future mixups. example:

Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
  IdentitiesOnly yes

ria: thanks everyone! tagging this resolved. shout if you want me to share a quick checklist in the onboarding doc for future new hires.

samir: please do — that would save a bunch of flip-flopping. can you paste the commands you ran into the onboarding doc once you're settled?

ria: will do later today. thanks again :pray:

people-ops: marking as resolved on our side — welcome to Redwood Inference, ria! :party:
